owner: CC owns the enforcement. Akien owns nothing here — the append door and PROVEME drift check are already physics; this is the residue they cannot reach.
intention: state/history files have an append door and a PROVEME drift check. Three things evade them: (1) an in-place edit of history itself — rewriting a past entry rather than appending; (2) at-rest components between voyages, whose state and history are not actively watched; (3) nothing notices history that has stopped being under way (Law 5's new bound — overlaps with history-reach-feeds-a-migration). This ticket closes the enforcement gaps so the append-only property and the under-way bound are physics, not policy.
why: The append door makes history append-only by routing new entries through a single writer. But the door does not prevent a direct file edit — 'echo > history.json' is invisible to the door. The PROVEME drift check catches unauthorized changes at crossing time, but a component at rest (between voyages) is never crossed, so its files can be edited with nothing noticing until the next voyage begins. And Law 5's new bound adds a third gap: even if the files are untouched, history that should have migrated to the commons but hasn't is still violating the working-surface promise.
traces_to: Law 5 — history of a thing under way belongs beside it; history past that berths in the commons.
Law 4 — append-only is a rule that matters; the door enforces it for appends but not for edits.
Law 7 — errors are loud and permanent in records of truth; an in-place edit of history silently changes a record of truth.

how.in_place_edit_check: A build_inspector sieve. For each history.json and state.json in the tree: load the file, load the LAST COMMITTED version via `git show HEAD:<path>`, and compare. The committed version is the ground truth — the append door writes and commits in one act. If an entry in the committed version is ABSENT or CHANGED in the working copy, that is an in-place edit. If the working copy has entries the committed version does not, that is an uncommitted append — a different finding (the append door should have committed it). The sieve shakes at every PROVEME crossing via build_inspector, AND at the ground_loop beat (gap 2 below).
how.at_rest_watch: The SAME sieve, but fired at the ground_loop beat rather than only at crossings. The beat already walks every shim; adding a git-diff check on state.json and history.json beside each charter is one more predicate per component, and it fires whether the component is mid-voyage or at rest. The cost is one `git show` per file per beat — bounded by the number of components with state/history files (currently 33 history.json). A component at rest whose files are silently edited gets flagged at the next beat, not at the next voyage.
how.law_5_boundary_with_history_reach: This ticket owns gaps (1) and (2) — in-place edits and at-rest watch. Gap (3) — history that should have migrated to commons but hasn't — belongs to history-reach-feeds-a-migration. The boundary: this ticket checks whether files were TAMPERED WITH; that ticket checks whether files SHOULD STILL BE HERE. The two can share a sieve that runs both checks, but the findings are distinct and the migrations are distinct.

gates: A build_inspector sieve that detects in-place edits of state.json and history.json by comparing working copy against last committed version. The same sieve also fires at the ground_loop beat to catch edits to at-rest components between voyages. Proof teeth: (1) a fixture history.json with a modified past entry reds; (2) a fixture history.json with a new appended entry that was not committed flags as uncommitted-append; (3) an untouched history.json passes; (4) the check fires at the beat, not only at crossings.
falsifier: RED if: (1) an in-place edit of a history.json entry passes undetected; (2) an at-rest component's state.json is modified between voyages with nothing noticing; (3) the check only fires at crossing time — at-rest is the gap, and a check that requires a crossing to fire does not close it; (4) the overlap with history-reach-feeds-a-migration is unresolved — the boundary is drawn above: tampered-with vs should-still-be-here.
horizon: Shares a build surface with history-reach-feeds-a-migration. The in-place-edit check (git-based) is simpler and lands first.
dependencies: The existing append door (cairn/tools/base/transitions.py) — the enforcement this extends.
ground_loop — where the at-rest beat fires.
history-reach-feeds-a-migration — the companion ticket for Law 5's gap (3); boundary drawn in how.law_5_boundary_with_history_reach.
distinctions_recorded: APPEND DOOR vs IN-PLACE EDIT: the door routes NEW entries. It says nothing about old entries being rewritten. These are different write operations and need different enforcement.
AT-REST vs CROSSING: the PROVEME drift check fires at crossing time. A component that never crosses is never checked. The gap is temporal, not logical. The fix is the beat, which is unconditional.
TAMPERED-WITH vs SHOULD-STILL-BE-HERE: this ticket's question and history-reach-feeds-a-migration's question. Both read the same files; they ask different things about them.
